newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:

** The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 66.58 points, or 1.15 percent, at a record 5,838.52 on Friday, beating the old high of 5,778.00 set May 22 as fresh signs of moderate growth with little inflation raised hopes that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates.
** The Tokyo stock market is closed on Monday due to a public holiday.
** Armed Forces Chief General Feisal Tanjung has flatly rejected demands to reopen the investigation into a bloody riot in Jakarta's Tanjung Priok port district 12 years ago.

** The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.57 points, or 0.47 percent, to close at 549.04 points on Friday on the back of limited foreign-buying of selected big-capitalised stocks and active second-liners.
** Brokers said they expected more foreign buying on Monday after fears receded of a possible hike in U.S. interest rates.
** The Indonesian rupiah was at 2,323.80/24.50 in early Monday trading against an opening of 2,322.50/23.50.
** Telkom on news reports that the telecommunications giant expected revenue growth of 15-25 percent in 1996 and that the firm had no plans for an additional share flotation.

** Astra on market talk that the firm's founder was likely to rejoin the automobile conglomerate and on news reports that a subsidiary was likely to launch two new models of its popular Kijang vehicle.
** Bank Tiara and Bank Mashill on media reports that the two banks have submitted a merger proposal to the central bank.
** Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma on reports that the firm planned to announce a stock split and reduce its shareholding in subsidiary Igar Jaya.
